latest_findings.claim: At N=64, accel_step first reached the 0.1 margin at steps 85-90 in all 3 seeds. That is 45-75 steps before val_mse_ratio first fell below 1 (steps 135-165), so the ordering holds at the default bar. The hypothesis still fails on its other two parts. (1) In 2 of 3 seeds the accel_step margin never reached 0.15: it levelled off at 0.134-0.135 (final R2 0.884-0.904 vs best-of-5 control 0.750-0.770). In seed 48 it reached 0.150 at step 150, only 5 steps before val_mse_ratio < 1. (2) The early force spike survives best-of-5 controls in all 3 seeds. Force margin was 0.166-0.189 at step 10 and stayed at or above 0.1 through step 25 (seed 49 dipped to 0.099 at step 20). It then decayed to about 0.00-0.02 by step 40-50, and final force R2 was 0.485-0.523 vs control 0.440-0.464 (margin 0.039-0.059, which does not beat control).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Two of the expected-if-false conditions were met in all 3 seeds: accel_step stays below 0.15 in 2 seeds, and force reaches the required margin within steps 5-50 in all 3. Only the 0.1-threshold ordering part was supported, and that held in 3/3. The controls look fixed across checkpoints: trained R2 minus margin is about 0.44-0.47 at step 10 and at step 300 in every seed. So the force spike comes from the trained model's force R2 rising (about 0.37-0.47 at step 0 to 0.61-0.64 at step 10) and falling back, not from the control set drawing a low best-of-5. Caveat: control_spread is reported only for the final checkpoint (0.037-0.077 for force). The step-10 margins exceed this by about 0.09 or more, but per-checkpoint required_margin is not shown. With threshold-free measures the accel_step-first ordering still holds in 3/3 seeds. Half of the final margin is reached at steps 50-65, and a headroom-normalized margin of 0.5 or more is first reached at steps 100, 125 and 130, though in seed 49 that is only 5 steps before val_mse_ratio < 1. What would change the verdict: per-checkpoint control_spread above 0.17 at step 10, or a 0.15 bar crossed in more seeds with longer training. The accel_step margin is flat from step 200 to 300, so the second seems unlikely. The 0.15 bar sits near the N=64 accel_step ceiling because the control R2 is 0.72-0.77, so failing it says more about the bar than about timing.

latest_findings.claim: Under the pre-registered rule this test is inconclusive: the 6-layer, d_model=128 models at e in [0, 0.85] never reach the 0.8 accel_step R2 the rule requires. Best accel_step R2 is 0.706 (seed 53) and 0.701 (seed 52) at layer 6, against controls of 0.301 and 0.292, so the margins are 0.405 and 0.409. Force is lower: R2 0.562 and 0.498 at layer 6, controls 0.253 and 0.200, margins 0.309 and 0.298. Measured as a share of the headroom left above the control, accel_step leads force in both seeds (0.58 vs 0.41 in seed 53, 0.58 vs 0.37 in seed 52). Both models still predict well, with val_mse_ratio 0.0049 and 0.0052. Below that bar, the accel_step symbolic fits disagree between seeds. Seed 52 gives a^3/r^2, the true form, with fit_error 0.068, yet law_recovered is false. Seed 53 gives a^3/(r(0.20a + r)), whose r exponent moves between -1 and -2, with fit_error 0.281. Neither seed fits the a*(a/r - c) vis-viva form. The force fits stay at c/r in both seeds (fit_error 0.57 and 0.65).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps. The verdict is inconclusive because both seeds have accel_step R2 of about 0.70, under the pre-registered 0.8 bar, so the rule makes both seeds inconclusive rather than supporting or refuting. Taken at face value, the fits lean against an r^-1 encoding. Seed 52 meets the expected-if-true numbers except for the R2 bar (a^3/r^2, fit_error 0.068 < 0.2). Seed 53 is in between (fit_error 0.28, effective exponent between -1 and -2). Neither run returns the a*(a/r - c) form seen at e <= 0.7, which weakly suggests the earlier vis-viva fits came from the narrower eccentricity range. But these fits come from probe directions with R2 0.70, where earlier work suggests fitted forms are unreliable (q-20261011-223103-8047). The two seeds also give different forms, and we have no measure of how much a fit varies when rerun on the same run. Seed 52 reports law_recovered false despite fit_error 0.068, and that is unexplained. It may be gated on probe R2 or on the coefficient, and I have not checked which. The accel_step control R2 dropped from 0.71-0.76 at e <= 0.5 to 0.29-0.30 here, so margins here are not directly comparable with the low-eccentricity runs. What would change this: a readout that reaches R2 >= 0.8 at e <= 0.85, such as an MLP probe or a probe on log(accel_step), plus a fit to it recovering r^-2 in both seeds, would support the hypothesis. A fit that returns r^-1 or a*(a/r - c) there would refute it.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 with best-of-5 controls and checkpoints every 10 steps, accel_step first reaches its required margin of 0.1 at step 100, 110 and 120 in seeds 29, 50 and 51. All three fall inside the predicted [90, 150] window and match the N=64 range of steps 100-140. Final accel_step R2 is 0.882-0.904 at layer 3, against a control of 0.705-0.753 (margin 0.151-0.177, control spread <= 0.009). Force never beats its control at the end: R2 0.18-0.55, margin -0.001 to 0.056. Its only crossings are a short spike at steps 10-20 (margin 0.127-0.242) that fades below 0.1 by step 30-60. Meanwhile all three models stay 11.4-13.5x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Three completed seeds (none stopped) agree, so this replicates 'accel_step timing roughly fixed across steps_per_orbit'. The 'later at N=256' hypothesis from f-20261011-231210-478d is refuted at the 0.1 threshold. Several things limit this. (1) The margins at the moment of formation are right at the bar: 0.103, 0.109, and exactly 0.100 for seed 51. The accel_step margin rises smoothly from about 0 at step 0 and levels off at 0.15-0.18, so the 'formation step' is where a smooth ramp crosses a threshold, not a sharp event. At a stricter 0.15 bar, seed 29 crosses at step 150 but seeds 50 and 51 only at steps 230-240. That would push N=256 outside the N=64 window and could flip the verdict. (2) The N=64 comparison window (100-140) comes from earlier runs with best-of-3 controls and different seeds, not from a matched sweep in this experiment. (3) accel_step forms while val_mse_ratio is still 87-98. These models never beat the baseline, so this result says the accel_step margin is not tied to prediction quality at N=256. It says nothing about how the margin is used. (4) The control R2 for accel_step is high (0.71-0.75), so absolute headroom is small. The headroom-normalised margin is about 0.56-0.61 for accel_step versus 0.07-0.12 for force. What would change the verdict: a matched N=64/N=256 sweep with the same seeds and best-of-5 controls showing N=256 later at a 0.15 or headroom-normalised threshold.

latest_findings.claim: At 6 layers and d_model=128, both seeds encode accel_step strongly: R2 0.931 vs control 0.630 (seed 41, margin 0.30) and 0.915 vs 0.675 (seed 40, margin 0.24), both at layer 6. Force is weaker: R2 0.680 vs 0.429 and 0.761 vs 0.447 at layer 1, so accel_step leads on headroom-normalized margin (0.81/0.74 vs 0.44/0.57). The symbolic fit to accel_step still has the r^-1 form a*(a/r - c)*k, with c = 0.499 and 0.539, close to the vis-viva value 0.5. Its r exponent is -1 and its a exponent is 2, outside the predicted [-2.5, -1.5] and [2.5, 3.5]. Yet fit_error_vs_true_law is 0.178 and 0.161, below 0.2, and law_recovered is false in both. The force fits are also r^-1 (0.74/r and 0.80/r, error 0.47).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither predicted outcome happened in full. The expected-if-true branch fails on the exponents: r^-1 and a^2 persist despite about 4x more parameters (1.2M), so the capacity-limit idea is not supported on the fitted form. The expected-if-false branch fails on fit_error, which is below 0.2 in both seeds (0.161-0.178, compared with about 0.20 at the smaller size). Both seeds show the same mixed pattern, so this is not seed noise. The r^-1 form clearly survives scaling. What remains unclear is whether fit_error < 0.2 means anything here: for near-circular orbits, a^2/r - a/2 is proportional to a^3/r^2, so the error metric may not be able to tell the two laws apart at e <= 0.7. If fitting the same pipeline to the true accel_step target recovers r^-2 with low error, the verdict would move toward refuted (the model really encodes an r^-1 quantity). If the exact vis-viva form scores below 0.2 against the true law, the fit_error criterion cannot decide this hypothesis. Distance and energy do not beat their controls here (controls 0.89-0.91, margins 0.05-0.09). Each run is single-checkpoint (final only).

latest_findings.claim: Patching the top force-scoring head (force_r2 about 0.35) did not single out a gravity-specific pathway: its effect was 27.5 vs 16.6 for the control head in seed 43 (1.66x, inside the pre-registered 2x 'false' band) and 109.6 vs 46.5 in seed 42 (2.36x, short of the 3x bar), so the specificity prediction fails, though both heads cause very large MSE increases. Residual-stream probes replicate earlier m2-fixed runs: force R2 0.699/0.650 at layer 1 (margin 0.230/0.165 over control 0.469/0.485), accel_step R2 0.851/0.841 at layer 4 (margin 0.238/0.280); headroom-normalised margins favour accel_step (0.61/0.64 vs force 0.43/0.32); val_mse_ratio 0.018/0.014.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This refutes the pre-registered criterion because seed 43 falls within 2x of its control. It does not support the expected-if-false reading that the force head 'carries little that prediction depends on'. Every patch is destructive: the top head raises MSE 28-110x and even the lowest-scoring head raises it 17-47x. Cross-system activation swapping probably injects wrong orbit-scale (a) information into any head, which swamps head-specific effects. That makes this a weak test of whether the head is specific. Seed 42's 2.36x ratio is in the gap between the true and false criteria, so the two seeds do not independently agree. Each run patches only one top head and one control head, and heads are ranked by force R2, which is low at about 0.35. The verdict would change if a gentler intervention, such as mean-ablation, or patching from a system with matched a, gave the top head an effect at least 3x the control in both seeds, or if heads ranked by accel_step showed clear specificity. Probe margins are well above required_margin (0.1; control_spread <= 0.09) in both seeds, and both runs completed 3000/3000 steps.
